reasoning_traces.think:
The Halo method introduces a scale head to existing deep forecasters, enabling heteroscedastic estimation by jointly optimizing location and scale under NLL. This improves point estimates because it forces the model to learn data-dependent uncertainty, which in turn regularizes the mean prediction. The dual-head wiring offers computational efficiency while maintaining performance, and the rescaling mechanism ensures consistency under nonstationarity. The theoretical basis lies in the equivalence between minimizing NLL and maximizing likelihood under assumed distributions. In practice, this leads to better calibrated forecasts and improved accuracy, especially in volatile domains like electricity pricing. Failure modes include misalignment between scale and mean learning or insufficient capacity in the shared backbone to represent both components effectively.
